name: i2i
description: i2i Fulfillment is a Canadian omnichannel fulfillment and supply-chain partner with Vancouver and Toronto distribution centres. This app exposes read-only ship order lookups for the i2i IBIS API.

authentication.name: i2i HMAC API key
authentication.description: Uses the i2i API key as the HMAC SHA-256 signing secret. Requests are signed with X-Echo-Signature and X-Echo-User headers; the default bearer Authorization header is removed by the request mapper.
authentication.notes: The i2i API requires X-Echo-Signature = base64(HMAC-SHA256(apiKey, METHOD + path + UTC date + nonce)) and X-Echo-User = username:nonce. Keep this auth read-only for this app build.

credentials.name: Username
credentials.description: i2i username used in the X-Echo-User signing header.

arguments.name: Messages
arguments.description: An array of message objects of a single message or multiple messages sent under one bulk ID.

arguments.name: Sender
arguments.description:
Email address with optional sender name. 

 Note: This field is required if `templateId` is not present.

arguments.name: Destinations
arguments.description:
An array of destination objects for where messages are being sent. A valid destination is required.

 Note: Maximum number of recipients is 1000 overall including `to`, `cc` and `bcc` field.

arguments.name: Subject
arguments.description:
Message subject.

Note: This field is required if `templateId` is not present.

arguments.name: Html
arguments.description: The message's body in HTML format. If both `html` and `text` fields are included, the `text` field will be disregarded, and the message will be sent using the `html` content.

arguments.name: Amp Html
arguments.description: The message's body in AMP HTML format. If you include `ampHtml`, you must also include `html`, which will be displayed if AMP is not supported. Keep in mind that not all email clients support AMP HTML. For guidance on configuring the Gmail client, please visit this link: https://developers.google.com/gmail/ampemail/ .

arguments.name: Template Id
arguments.description:
The Template ID with predefined email content created through the Infobip web interface or API. When `templateId` is specified, the `html` and `text` fields will be disregarded.

Note: `templateId` only supports the `Broadcast` value; `Content` and `Flow` templates are not supported.

arguments.name: Inline Images
arguments.description: Allows for inserting an image file inside the HTML code of the email by using `cid:FILENAME` instead of providing an external link to the image.

arguments.name: Default Placeholders
arguments.description: General placeholders: `{"ph1": "Success"}` will replace the key `{{ph1}}` with the value Success throughout the email, including the `subject`, `text`, and HTML. If there are multiple recipients in the To field, this placeholder will use the same value for the key ph1 for all recipients.

arguments.name: Landing Page Placeholders
arguments.description: Personalize Opt-Out Landing Page by inserting placeholders. Insert placeholder or tag while designing landing page. Value should be defined as: `{"unsubscribe": "Unsubscribe"}`

arguments.name: Optout Landing Page Id
arguments.description: The Opt-Out Landing Page ID specifies the page to be displayed when an end user clicks the unsubscribe link. If the ID is not provided, the default opt-out landing page will be used. Create a landing page over Infobip web interface and use its ID, for example, `1_23456.`

arguments.name: Template Language Version
arguments.description: Indicates the version of the template language to be used in the current message template. Use version 1 for the older template language and version 2 to access features of the new template language. If not specified, version 1 will be used by default.

arguments.name: Headers
arguments.description:
Additional email headers for customization that can be provided in a form of JSON. Example: `headers={"X-CustomHeader": "Header value"}`.

There are a few exceptions of headers which are not adjustable through this option: `To`, `Cc`, `Bcc`, `From`, `Subject`, `Content-Type`, `DKIM-Signature`, `Content-Transfer-Encoding`, `Return-Path`, `MIME-Version`

arguments.name: Platform
arguments.description: Platform options. For more details, see [documentation](https://www.infobip.com/docs/cpaas-x/application-and-entity-management).

arguments.name: Validity Period
arguments.description: Message validity period. Once expired, the message won't be sent. Validity period longer than 48h is not supported. If exceeded, it will be automatically set to 48h.

arguments.name: Delivery Time Window
arguments.description: Sets specific message delivery window outside of which messages won't be delivered. Often, used when there are restrictions on when messages can be sent. The exact time of the day to start sending messages can be defined using the `from` property. The exact time of the day to end sending messages can be defined using the `to` property. Properties `from` and `to` should be both provided with the minimum 1 hour difference or omitted.

arguments.name: Content Type
arguments.description: Preferred delivery report content type, `application/json` or `application/xml`.

arguments.name: Callback Data
arguments.description: Additional data that can be used for identifying, managing, or monitoring a message. Data included here will also be automatically included in the message Delivery Report. The maximum value is 4000 characters.

arguments.name: Ip Pool Id
arguments.description: The ID of the IP pool that will be used to send the email.

arguments.name: Placeholders Masking
arguments.description: Options to full or partially mask placeholders.

arguments.name: Skip Passive
arguments.description:
Set to true to skip [passive email storage](https://www.infobip.com/docs/email/email-storage-and-retrieval/passive-email-storage) (long-term storage used for compliance, legal, or audit purposes).
            If `false` or not set, the account-level setting is used.

arguments.name: Skip Active
arguments.description:
Set to true to skip [active email storage](https://www.infobip.com/docs/email/email-storage-and-retrieval/active-email-storage) (short-term storage used for troubleshooting or support).
            If `false` or not set, the account-level setting is used.

arguments.name: Options
arguments.description: Options applicable to all messages in the request.

arguments.name: Bulk Id
arguments.description: Unique ID assigned to the request if messaging multiple recipients or sending multiple messages via a single API request. If not provided, it will be auto-generated and returned in the API response.

arguments.name: Send At
arguments.description: Date and time when the message is to be sent. Used for scheduled messages. Has the following format: `yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSSZ`, and can only be scheduled for no later than 5 days in advance.

arguments.name: Track
arguments.description: Enable or disable open and click tracking. Passing true will only enable tracking and the statistics will be visible in the web interface alone. This can be explicitly overridden by `trackClicks` and `trackOpens`.

arguments.name: Track Opens
arguments.description: This parameter enables or disables track open feature.

arguments.name: Track Clicks
arguments.description: This parameter enables or disables track click feature.

arguments.name: Tracking Url
arguments.description: The URL on your callback server on which the open and click notifications will be sent. See [Tracking Notifications](https://www.infobip.com/docs/email/send-email-over-api#tracking-notifications) for details.

arguments.name: Tracking Pixel Position
arguments.description: This parameter specifies the position of the open tracking pixel within the email content. Allowed values are `TOP` and `BOTTOM`. If no value is provided, the default is `TOP`.

arguments.name: Client Priority
arguments.description: Client priority set on request. Must be 'HIGH', 'STANDARD' or 'LOW'.

arguments.name: From
arguments.description:
Email address with optional sender name.

Note: This field is required if `templateId` is not present.

arguments.name: To
arguments.description:
Email address of the recipient in a form of `To="john.smith@somecompany.com"`.
As optional feature on this field, a specific placeholder can be defined whose value will apply only for this destination. Given `To` value should look like:
`To= {"to": "john.smith@somecompany.com","placeholders": {"name": "John"}}`
`To= {"to": "alice.grey@somecompany.com","placeholders": {"name": "Alice"}}`.

Note: Maximum number of recipients per request is 1000 overall including to, cc and bcc field.

arguments.name: Cc
arguments.description:
CC recipient email address.
As optional feature on this field, a specific placeholder can be defined whose value will apply only for this destination.

Note: Maximum number of recipients per request is 1000 overall including to, cc and bcc field.

arguments.name: Bcc
arguments.description:
BCC recipient email address.
As optional feature on this field, a specific placeholder can be defined whose value will apply only for this destination.

Note: Maximum number of recipients per request is 1000 overall including to, cc and bcc field.

arguments.name: Subject
arguments.description:
Message subject.

Note: This field is required if `templateId` is not present.

arguments.name: Html
arguments.description: HTML body of the message. If `html` and `text` fields are present, the `text` field will be ignored and `html` will be delivered as a message body.

arguments.name: Amp Html
arguments.description: Amp HTML body of the message. If `ampHtml` is present, `html` is mandatory. Amp HTML is not supported by all the email clients. Please check this link for configuring gmail client https://developers.google.com/gmail/ampemail/.

arguments.name: Template Id
arguments.description:
Template ID used for generating email content. The template is created over Infobip web interface or via the [Infobip Templates API](https://www.infobip.com/docs/api/channels/email/templates). If `templateId` is present, then `html` and `text` values are ignored.

Note: `templateId` only supports the value of `Broadcast`. `Content` and `Flow` are not supported.

arguments.name: Inline Image
arguments.description: Allows for inserting an image file inside the HTML code of the email by using `cid:FILENAME` instead of providing an external link to the image.

arguments.name: Intermediate Report
arguments.description: The real-time Intermediate delivery report that will be sent on your callback server.

arguments.name: Notify Url
arguments.description: The URL on your callback server on which the Delivery report will be sent.

arguments.name: Notify Content Type
arguments.description: Preferred Delivery report content type. Can be `application/json` or `application/xml`.

arguments.name: Callback Data
arguments.description: Additional client data that will be sent on the notifyUrl.

arguments.name: Track
arguments.description: Enable or disable open and click tracking. Passing true will only enable tracking and the statistics would be visible in the web interface alone. This can be explicitly overridden by `trackClicks` and `trackOpens`.

arguments.name: Track Clicks
arguments.description:
This parameter enables or disables track click feature.

Note: Option to disable click tracking per URL is available. For detailed usage, please refer to the [documentation](https://www.infobip.com/docs/email/email-tracking-and-analytics/email-tracking-types#disable-click-tracking-on-urls-url-clicks).

arguments.name: Track Opens
arguments.description: This parameter enables or disables track open feature.

arguments.name: Tracking Pixel Position
arguments.description:
This parameter specifies the position of the open tracking pixel within the email content.
Allowed values are `TOP` and `BOTTOM`. If no value is provided, the default is `TOP`.

arguments.name: Tracking Url
arguments.description: The URL on your callback server on which the open and click notifications will be sent. See [Tracking Notifications](https://www.infobip.com/docs/email/email-over-api/tracking-notifications) for details.

arguments.name: Bulk Id
arguments.description: The ID that uniquely identifies the sent bulk. This filter will enable you to query delivery reports for all the messages using just one request. You will receive a `bulkId` in the response after sending an email request. If you don't set your own `bulkId`, unique ID will be generated by our system and returned in the API response. (Optional Field)

arguments.name: Message Id
arguments.description: The ID that uniquely identifies the message sent to a recipient. (Optional Field)

arguments.name: Campaign Reference Id
arguments.description: The ID that allows you to track, analyze, and show an aggregated overview and the performance of individual campaigns.

arguments.name: Reply To
arguments.description: Email address to which recipients of the email can reply.

arguments.name: Default Placeholders
arguments.description: General placeholder, given in a form of json example: `defaultPlaceholders={"ph1": "Success"}`, which will replace given key `{{ph1}}` with given value `Success` anywhere in the email (subject, text, html...). In case of more destinations in `To` field, this placeholder will resolve the same value for key `ph1`.

arguments.name: Preserve Recipients
arguments.description: If set to `true`, the `to` recipients will see the list of all other recipients to get the email and the response will return only one `messageId`. Otherwise, each recipient will see just their own email and the response will return a unique `messageId` for each email recipient.

arguments.name: Send At
arguments.description: To schedule message at a given time. Time provided should be in UTC in the following format: `yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSSZ` and cannot exceed 30 days in the future.

arguments.name: Landing Page Placeholders
arguments.description: Personalize opt out landing page by inserting placeholders. Insert placeholder or tag while designing landing page.

arguments.name: Landing Page Id
arguments.description: The ID of an opt out landing page to be used and displayed once an end user clicks the unsubscribe link. If not present, default opt out landing page will be displayed. Create a landing page in your Infobip account and use its ID, e.g., `1_23456`.

arguments.name: Template Language Version
arguments.description: Specifies template language version that will be used in the current message template. Use version 1 for previous version of template language. Use version 2 for features of the new template language. If not present version 1 will be used as default version.

arguments.name: Client Priority
arguments.description:
Adds a priority rating to this email message.
Allowed values are `HIGH`, `STANDARD` and `LOW`.
Messages with a higher priority value sent by your account are prioritized over messages with a lower priority value sent by your account.
If no priority value is provided, messages will be treated with `STANDARD` priority by default.

arguments.name: Application Id
arguments.description: Required for application use in a send request for outbound traffic. Returned in notification events.

arguments.name: Entity Id
arguments.description: Required for entity use in a send request for outbound traffic. Returned in notification events.

arguments.name: Headers
arguments.description:
Additional email headers for customization that can be provided in a form of JSON. For example, you can override List-Unsubscribe header and provide your own custom one: `headers={"List-Unsubscribe": "your unsubscribe link", "X-CustomHeader": "Header value"}`.

There are a few exceptions of headers which are not adjustable through this option: `To`, `Cc`, `Bcc`, `From`, `Subject`,`Content-Type`, `DKIM-Signature`, `Content-Transfer-Encoding`, `Return-Path`, `MIME-Version`

arguments.name: Messages
arguments.description: An array of message objects of a single message or multiple messages sent under one bulk ID.

arguments.name: Sender
arguments.description: The sender ID. It can be alphanumeric or numeric (e.g., `CompanyName`). Make sure you don't exceed [character limit](https://www.infobip.com/docs/sms/get-started#sender-names).

arguments.name: Destinations
arguments.description: An array of destination objects for where messages are being sent. A valid destination is required.

arguments.name: Platform
arguments.description: Platform options. For more details, see [documentation](https://www.infobip.com/docs/cpaas-x/application-and-entity-management).

arguments.name: Validity Period
arguments.description: Message validity period. Once expired, the message won't be sent. Validity period longer than 48h is not supported. If exceeded, it will be automatically set to 48h.

arguments.name: Delivery Time Window
arguments.description: Sets specific message delivery window outside of which messages won't be delivered. Often, used when there are restrictions on when messages can be sent. The exact time of the day to start sending messages can be defined using the `from` property. The exact time of the day to end sending messages can be defined using the `to` property. Properties `from` and `to` should be both provided with the minimum 1 hour difference or omitted.

arguments.name: Campaign Reference Id
arguments.description: ID that allows you to track, analyze, and show an aggregated overview and the performance of individual campaigns per sending channel.

arguments.name: Regional
arguments.description: Region-specific parameters, often imposed by local laws. Use this, if country or region that you are sending an SMS to requires additional information.

arguments.name: Flash
arguments.description: Allows for sending a [flash SMS](https://www.infobip.com/docs/sms/message-types#flash-sms) to automatically appear on recipient devices without interaction. Set to `true` to enable flash SMS, or leave the default value, `false` to send a standard SMS.

arguments.description: Unique ID assigned to the request if messaging multiple recipients or sending multiple messages via a single API request. If not provided, it will be auto-generated and returned in the API response.

arguments.name: Send At
arguments.description: Date and time when the message is to be sent. Used for scheduled messages. Has the following format: `yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSSZ`, and can only be scheduled for no later than 180 days in advance.

arguments.name: Sending Speed Limit
arguments.description: Limits the send speed when sending messages in bulk to deliver messages over a longer period of time. You may wish to use this to allow your systems or agents to handle large amounts of incoming traffic, e.g., if you are expecting recipients to follow through with a call-to-action option from a message you sent. Not setting a send speed limit can overwhelm your resources with incoming traffic.

arguments.name: Amount
arguments.description: The number of messages to be sent per timeUnit. By default, the system sends messages as fast as the infrastructure allows. Use this parameter to adapt sending capacity to your needs. The system is only able to work against its maximum capacity for ambitious message batches.

arguments.name: Time Unit
arguments.description: The time unit to define when setting a messaging speed limit. Defaults to `MINUTE`.

arguments.name: Shorten Url
arguments.description: Enable shortening of the URLs within a message. Set this to `true`, if you want to set up other URL options.

arguments.name: Track Clicks
arguments.description: Enable tracking of short URL clicks within a message: which URL was clicked, how many times, and by whom.

arguments.name: Tracking Url
arguments.description: The URL of your callback server on to which the Click report will be sent.

arguments.name: Remove Protocol
arguments.description: Remove a protocol, such as `https://`, from links to shorten a message. Note that some mobiles may not recognize such links as a URL.

arguments.name: Custom Domain
arguments.description: Select a predefined custom domain to use when generating a short URL.

arguments.name: Include Sms Count In Response
arguments.description: Set to true to return `messageCount` in the response. The `messageCount` is the total count of SMS submitted in the request. SMS messages have a character limit and messages longer than the limit will be split into multiple SMS. Not compatible with `binary` message content type.

arguments.name: Conversion Tracking
arguments.description: Allows you to set up tracking parameters to track conversion metrics. For more details, see: [SMS with conversion tracking](https://www.infobip.com/docs/sms/sms-over-api#send-sms-with-conversion-tracking).

arguments.name: Use Conversion Tracking
arguments.description: Indicates if a message has to be tracked for conversion rates. Default "false".

arguments.name: Conversion Tracking Name
arguments.description: Sets a custom conversion type naming convention, e.g. `ONE_TIME_PIN` or `SOCIAL_INVITES`.

steps.title: Paste the key in MindCloud
steps.description: Use the API Key field when creating the Infoplus connection. MindCloud sends the value in the Infoplus API-Key HTTP header.

steps.title: Confirm Reporting API access

setupGuide.title: How to set up your connection?
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: Use this connection only for your own Intercom workspace. If you need to access another company’s Intercom data, use OAuth instead.

steps.title: Open the Intercom Developer Hub
steps.description: Sign in to the Intercom workspace you want to connect, then open the Developer Hub for that workspace.

steps.title: Open your Intercom app
steps.description: Go to Your Apps and select the app you want to use for this private connection.

steps.title: Find the Access Token
steps.description: Open the Authentication section of the app and copy the Access Token shown there. Intercom provides this token when you create an app on your workspace.

steps.title: Paste the token into the connection form
steps.description: Return to the connection form and paste the value into the Access Token field.

name: Intradesk
description: Intradesk is an IT service management platform for service desk tickets, workflows, users, clients, assets, knowledge base content, and operational reporting.

authentication.name: Bearer Access Token
authentication.description: Connect Intradesk using a bearer access token. Intradesk documents access-token auth through the token endpoint and supports refresh-token-capable scopes via offline_access.
authentication.notes: Auth method: Bearer access token. Refresh token available via Intradesk token endpoint scope `offline_access`; configure credentials with a valid Intradesk access token and refresh token for runtime refresh. Provider docs use password-grant token acquisition, while MindCloud keeps this as OAuth2 to support refresh-token execution.

name: Invoice Ninja
description: Create invoices, manage clients, track expenses, and get paid

authentication.name: API Key
authentication.description: Authenticate using X-API-TOKEN and the required X-Requested-With header.

credentials.name: Base URL
credentials.description: Enter the full Invoice Ninja API root, including /api/v1.

setupGuide.title: Connect Invoice Ninja
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need an Invoice Ninja account with API access and a generated API token.

steps.title: Sign in to Invoice Ninja
steps.description: Sign in to the Invoice Ninja account you want to connect in MindCloud.

steps.title: Open API Tokens
steps.description: Go to Settings > Account Management > Integrations > API Tokens.

steps.title: Create and copy an API token
steps.description: Create a token and copy it right away. You will paste it into MindCloud as the API key.

steps.title: Choose the API base URL
steps.description: Use the full API root for your account: https://invoicing.co/api/v1 for hosted production, https://demo.invoiceninja.com/api/v1 for the public demo, or your self-hosted /api/v1 URL.

steps.title: Finish the MindCloud connection
steps.description: Paste the API token as the API key and enter the API base URL. MindCloud sends the required X-Requested-With header automatically.

name: Invoice.xhub
description: Generate, parse, and validate electronic invoices across 14 European countries with country-specific formats such as ZUGFeRD, XRechnung, Factur-X, UBL, QR-Bill, and FatturaPA.

authentication.name: API Key
authentication.description: Use an Invoice.xhub API key with the provider's bearer Authorization header contract.
authentication.notes: Invoice.xhub requires the API key in the Authorization header as a Bearer token. Live keys start with sk_live_ and test keys start with sk_test_.

setupGuide.title: Connect your Invoice.xhub account
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need an Invoice.xhub account and an API key from the Invoice.xhub console.

steps.title: Open the Invoice.xhub console
steps.description: Sign in to the Invoice.xhub console where API keys are managed.

steps.title: Create or copy an API key
steps.description: In the console, open your API key management area and either create a new key or copy an existing one. Use a live key for production access or a test key for sandbox testing.

steps.title: Paste the key into the MindCloud connection form
steps.description: Use the full Invoice.xhub API key as the connection credential. MindCloud stores it securely and sends it automatically as a Bearer token in the Authorization header.

setupGuide.title: Connect IP2Location IO
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need an IP2Location.io account and an API key for authenticated geolocation requests.

steps.title: Create an IP2Location.io account
steps.description: Sign up for the IP2Location.io free plan. The official docs say registration gives you an API key for authenticated geolocation requests.

steps.title: Complete account verification

steps.title: Copy your API key
steps.description: IP2Location.io documents that authenticated requests can use your API key either as a bearer token or as the key query parameter.

steps.title: Paste the API key into MindCloud
steps.description: Add the API key to the IP2Location IO connection in MindCloud and save the connection.

description: Look up IP geolocation, domain WHOIS, and hosted domains by IP with IP2Location.io and IP2WHOIS. Bulk IP geolocation is available on supported provider plans.

authentication.name: API Key
authentication.description: Use an IP2Location.io API key. MindCloud sends it as the required query parameter named key.

setupGuide.title: Connect your IP2Location.io account
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need an active IP2Location.io account and an API key for the IP2Location.io APIs.

steps.title: Create or sign in to your IP2Location.io account
steps.description: If you do not already have an account, register for a free IP2Location.io plan. If you already have one, sign in to the same account you want MindCloud to use.

steps.title: Copy your API key from your IP2Location.io account area
steps.description: Open your IP2Location.io account area and copy the API key for the account plan you want to use. MindCloud uses that key for IP geolocation, domain WHOIS, and hosted-domain requests.

steps.title: Paste the API key into MindCloud
steps.description: When MindCloud asks for your API key, paste the value exactly as shown in your IP2Location.io account area and save the connection.

name: Iris Dfir
description: IRIS is an incident response and DFIR collaboration platform for managing cases, alerts, IOCs, assets, evidences, tasks, comments, and related response workflows.

authentication.name: API Key
authentication.description: Connect Iris Dfir using the API key from My settings in the IRIS web app.
authentication.notes: Use the API key from `My settings` in IRIS. The platform injects it as `Authorization: Bearer {{credentials.apiKey}}`. The provider notes that renewing the key revokes the previous token, and the official demo instance may reset at any moment.

setupGuide.title: How to connect Iris Dfir

steps.title: Open My settings

steps.title: Copy the API key
steps.description: Copy the API key exactly as shown. If you renew it in IRIS, the previous key is revoked immediately.

steps.title: Paste the key into MindCloud
steps.description: Return to the MindCloud connection form and paste the API key into the API Key field.

name: ITM Platform
description: Project, program, and portfolio management software for planning, delivery, resources, risks, financials, and reporting in ITM Platform.

authentication.name: API Key
authentication.description: Connect with your ITM Platform company URL and API key.
authentication.notes: Provide your ITM Platform company URL segment and API key. The company value is the account slug used in API paths, for example `mycompany` in `https://api.itmplatform.com/v2/mycompany/projects/search`. The current public docs conflict on whether business calls accept the raw API key in `Token` or require exchanging it first via `GET /login/{APIKey}`; runtime verification stays blocked until the company value is available.

name: iubenda
description: Connect to the iubenda Consent Database HTTP API to manage consents, subjects, legal notices, and consent proof documents.

authentication.name: API Key
authentication.description: Use the iubenda Consent Database private API key for HTTP API requests.

setupGuide.title: Connect your iubenda Consent Database private API key
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need access to the iubenda dashboard for the site or app that owns the Consent Database.

steps.title: Open the Consent Database area in iubenda
steps.description: Sign in to iubenda, open the dashboard for the site or app you want to connect, then open Consent Database.

steps.title: Open the HTTP API tab
steps.description: In Consent Database, open Embed and then choose the HTTP API tab.

steps.title: Copy the private API key
steps.description: Copy the private API key shown in the HTTP API tab. The Consent Database HTTP API docs state that private-key requests must send the key in the ApiKey header.

steps.title: Paste the key into MindCloud
steps.description: Return to MindCloud and paste that private API key into the API key field for this connection.
